title: From Delisted to Sold: How a Fresh Marketing Strategy Helped Find the Right Buyer
summary: After nearly 800 days on the market, a Boston luxury home found its buyer through a refreshed narrative, strategic marketing and a focus on what makes the property truly unique.
body_markdown:
When a home sits on the market for an extended time, it can be easy to assume price may be the issue. But according to Andrew Veneziano with REMAX Andrew Realty Services in Medford, Massachusetts, that’s not always the case.


Recently, Veneziano took over the listing of a distinctive Boston property that spent nearly 800 days on the market across two separate listing periods. Despite the home’s prime location and luxury features, a buyer never materialized. That’s when the sellers sought out Veneziano to relist the home.


A situation like this offers an important reminder: When relisting a property, finding the right buyer often comes from rethinking the story, refreshing the marketing strategy and helping buyers see what makes a home truly special.


**Start by Understanding Why the Seller Fell in Love with the Home**


Before developing a marketing plan, Veneziano took a step back and asked the sellers a simple question: “Why did you buy this home in the first place?”


The previous listings, under prior real estate agents, highlighted features and specifications but failed to communicate what made the property unique: its rare combination of privacy, location and modern architecture in the heart of Boston.


“A lot of what the sellers loved about the home were the same things I saw when I walked through it myself,” Veneziano says. “Those weren’t really being talked about in the previous marketing materials.”


Rather than competing with other luxury homes on square footage or finishes alone, Veneziano highlighted the property’s distinctive identity as a contemporary take on a classic Boston row house near some of the city’s most recognizable destinations.


**A Fresh Story Creates Fresh Interest**


One of the biggest challenges with any relisting is overcoming buyer perception.


When a property has been available for months, or sometimes even years, buyers may assume something must be wrong.


That’s why Veneziano took on the listing with a completely new approach.


The property received updated marketing materials, new photography, a dedicated website and a refreshed digital presence designed to expand its visibility across multiple platforms.


“You never know where the buyer is going to come from,” Veneziano says. “It could be social media, a Google search, an agent referral or someone seeing an article of the listing online. The goal is to create as many opportunities as possible for someone to discover the home.”


The visual strategy also shifted dramatically.


Instead of leading with an interior photo that could have belonged to almost any luxury residence, the relaunch featured a twilight exterior image showcasing the home’s architecture and setting.


“The lead photo should tell the story,” Veneziano explains. “It should immediately show buyers what makes that property different from everything else on the market.”


**Reevaluate How Buyers Experience the Property**


Beyond marketing, Veneziano also reimagined how buyers would experience the home when they came for an open house or private walkthrough.


The property had previously been presented with a mix of furnishings and vacant spaces, making it difficult for visitors to understand the scale and flow.


For the relaunch, nearly all furnishings were removed, with only a few key pieces strategically placed to help define larger areas.


Rather than controlling the showing, Veneziano focused on thoughtfully guiding buyers through the home. He often began by asking how they envisioned using the property and even how they would typically arrive each day. Would they be walking from the neighborhood? Using the home as a primary residence or a second home? Would they enter through the front door or the garage? Did they have children? What did their day-to-day lifestyle look like?


“I asked every agent how their buyers would actually use the home,” Veneziano says. “The experience can be very different depending on whether it’s a family’s primary residence or a second home.”


By helping buyers picture their day-to-day routines in the home, the tours felt less like a sales presentation and more like an opportunity to see if the property truly fit their lifestyle.


Veneziano also refreshed the home’s presentation, including professional cleaning and landscaping improvements before capturing updated photography. Fresh spring imagery replaced older winter photos, helping ensure the online presentation felt current.


“We wanted everything to feel fresh,” Veneziano says. “People should walk in and immediately feel like the home is ready for them.”


Detailed brochures, virtual staging imagery, and floor-by-floor amenity sheets supplemented the MLS listing to help buyers fully understand the property’s features.


**Pricing Can Be a Tool, Not Just a Number**


While marketing played a critical role, pricing adjustments also helped reignite interest.


After evaluating market feedback and discussing strategy with the sellers, Veneziano recommended a reduction from the home’s previous asking price.


Rather than simply reducing the price, Veneziano repositioned the home at a level that created an opportunity to reengage buyers and build fresh momentum.


“A price adjustment tells buyers there’s a new opportunity and a new conversation happening,” Veneziano says. “It helps create momentum and shows the seller is willing to engage.”


The adjustment generated renewed interest and ultimately helped attract the eventual buyers who submitted a strong cash offer with favorable terms.


**Lean Into What Makes a Property Different**


Looking back, Veneziano believes the most impactful change was identifying and embracing the home’s distinct value proposition.


Too often, agents market homes by focusing on features that many properties for sale have in common. Buyers, however, are frequently looking for something unique that fits their lifestyle.


“There are a lot of beautiful homes with nice kitchens and great finishes,” he says. “The question is: What’s the whole package? What makes this home different?”


For this property, the answer wasn’t trying to make it feel like a traditional Boston row house. It was celebrating the fact that it wasn’t.


“That’s exactly why the buyers purchased it,” Veneziano says. “We weren’t looking for someone who wanted what everyone else had. We were looking for the buyer who wanted a modern home in this location.”


**The Power of the REMAX Network**


Veneziano also credits the broader REMAX network and The REMAX Collection® for expanding the property’s reach.


Marketing resources, luxury branding support, peer collaboration, and referral opportunities helped expose the listing to buyers and agents well beyond the local market.


“The REMAX brand gave the property additional visibility,” Veneziano says. “Between referrals, luxury expertise within the network, and national and international exposure, we were able to reach audiences we might not have otherwise connected with.”


**Takeaways for Agents Relisting a Luxury Home**


For agents facing a listing that previously struggled to sell, Veneziano’s approach offers a simple lesson: Don’t assume the original strategy was telling the right story. Instead:


- Reevaluate what makes the property unique.
- Ask sellers why they fell in love with the home.
- Refresh marketing assets and photography.
- Consider how buyers experience the property in-person.
- Use pricing strategically to create momentum.


After all, in real estate, it takes only one buyer who understands the value of what makes a property special.


And sometimes, finding that buyer starts with telling a better story.
